title: Slotized credit allocation playbook (back-of-envelope)
content:
Purpose:
Quick notebook to explore a slot-based credit system that maps capacity (concurrency + warm state) to credits rather than purely per-token billing. Aim: cleaner SLO signal for customers with bursty conversational workloads and simpler amortization of GPU-hour fixed costs. This is intentionally BOTE (back-of-the-envelope) — lots of assumptions flagged below.

Key concepts / units:
- slot-minute: one concurrency slot held for one minute. A slot represents reserved capacity to accept/serve low-latency requests (maintains KV cache and model readiness).
- credit: currency unit we sell to customers. Proposal: price credits to cover both per-token compute and slot maintenance.
- token-credit conversion: for initial sketch, 1 credit ~= 100 tokens (purely arbitrary mapping to keep integers tidy).

Assumptions (explicit):
- cloud GPU cost: $3.00 / GPU-hour (back-of-envelope; use provider + infra overhead later)
- model throughput (gen only): 1.2M tokens / GPU-hour for a small-ish quantized model (this is optimistic; pick conservative buckets later)
- per-token pure compute cost = 3 / 1,200,000 = $0.0000025 per token = $0.00025 per 100 tokens = $0.00025 per credit (if 1 credit = 100 tokens)
- slot maintenance: if we keep a warm slot pinned on a GPU, we amortize some fraction of GPU-minute cost to it. 1 GPU-hour = 60 GPU-minutes -> $3/60 = $0.05 per GPU-minute. If a slot ties up 1/8th of a GPU for caching (toy number), cost per slot-minute = $0.05/8 = $0.00625.

Mapping slot -> credits (sketch):
- baseline token provision inside a slot-minute: expect X tokens generated per minute when slot gets requests. But many slots are idle for some minutes — need hybrid billing: charge small per-slot-minute credit + per-token credit when used.
- propose: slot-minute base charge = 25 credits (covers ~25 * 100 = 2500 tokens' worth of amortized compute + cache maintenance buffer) -> $0.00025 * 25 = $0.00625 which aligns to the example slot-minute cost above. Nice coincidence.
- per-token consumption above included amount billed at token-credit rate (1 credit/100 tokens).

Example scenarios:
1) Low-traffic chat bot (sparse requests)
   - 1 active user on average, 10 messages/day, mostly idle rest of time.
   - If we provision 1 slot for convenience and keep it warm: slot-minute cost = 25 credits/min * 60 * 24 = 36,000 credits/day (obviously crazy if we charge full time). For personal users we need a different policy: auto-suspend after idle threshold (e.g., 10 minutes) to avoid massive slot charges.
   - For contended enterprise, slots make sense when they reduce tail-latency and avoid repeated cold-starts.

2) SaaS with bursty interaction (conversational app)
   - Typical pattern: idle for long stretches, bursts of 200 requests/min for 2–5 minutes. Without slots you'd pay per-token compute + cold-start overhead. With slots: keep N slots available to cover peak concurrent sessions.
   - Suppose peak concurrency 50 -> keep 50 slots during bursts. If we charge 25 credits/slot-minute, burst cost per minute = 50 * 25 = 1,250 credits -> converted to USD at token-equivalent: 1,250 credits * $0.00025 = $0.3125 per minute of peak capacity. If bursts last 5 minutes and occur 10x/day -> daily slot cost = 0.3125 * 5 * 10 = $15.625 plus per-token usage for messages/responses. Seems sane for mid-market app.

Per-token vs slot hybrid math (rough):
- Per-token compute: 1 credit per 100 tokens -> $0.00025 per credit. So 10k tokens = 100 credits = $0.025 compute.
- If a slot-minute already charges 25 credits, that buys ~2.5k tokens-worth of compute in the minute. If usage in that minute < 2.5k tokens, customer effectively subsidizes idle warm state. If usage > 2.5k tokens, excess billed at 1 credit/100 tokens.

Edge-case approaches:
- auto-suspend slots after an idle window (10–30m) to avoid 24/7 charges for low-activity users.
- short-duration burst credits: let customers buy minute-bundles at a discount (e.g., 60 slot-minutes bundle at 15% off) to handle predictable peaks.
- per-route SLO override: some routes see critical low-latency; mark them "high-slot" and charge higher slot-minute price.

Unit-econ back-of-envelope (monthly per-customer):
- model: small startup with 5k MAUs, average 4 convo messages/day (so ~20k messages/day). Assume each message cycle uses 80 tokens (request+response): 20k * 80 = 1.6M tokens/day -> 48M tokens/month.
- Using per-token compute only: 48M tokens / 100 * 1 credit = 480k credits -> $0.00025 * 480k = $120 / month (compute-only)
- If we require 200 slots for peak concurrency for short bursts: assume 200 slots * 25 credits/slot-minute * 5 min bursts * 30 bursts/month = 200 * 25 * 5 * 30 = 750k credits = $187.5. Total = $307.5/mo (combined).
- This highlights slots can dominate costs for bursty but highly concurrent workloads; need careful defaults and autoscaling.

Questions / Unknowns to validate next: 
- real measured tokens/GPU-hour for the set of curated models we offer (we need profile table per model + quantization level).
- realistic fraction of GPU reserved when holding a slot (1/8th used above is arbitrary). For some setups a slot is cheap (shared across many tenants) if KV cache is in host RAM not full GPU memory.
- how often slots will be idle vs hot — we need P99, median idle durations across sample customers.
- UX: how much complexity will customers accept (slot-minutes + per-token)? Could present simplified bundles: e.g., "conversational plan" includes 1k slot-minutes + X token credits.

Behavioral considerations (notes to self):
- customers care about predictability: offer a monthly slot allowance that smooths spend.
- give a free auto-burst allowance (small slot pool) to avoid friction for trial users; suspend if long-term idle.
- present visualizer in Console: slot usage heatmap (minutes used, average idle time, wasted slot-minutes).

Immediate next steps / experiments: 
- instrument 10 production customers for 30 days to capture request concurrency over time, idle distributions, per-request token counts. Ticket -> PRIC-212.
- run microbench to measure tokens/GPU-hour across our top 4 models/quant levels. Ticket -> PERF-453.
- prototype billing UI that shows combined slot-minute + token burn and a "what-if" slider for slot count.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] compute per-model token/GPU-hour and populate model profile table (owner: @Ethan)
- [ ] simulate cost for 10 customer archetypes (low, bursty, chatty, embedding-heavy) (owner: @Priya)
- [ ] draft customer-friendly phrasing for slot concept and auto-suspend defaults (owner: me)

Random thoughts / brain-dump (unfiltered):
- Maybe allow "micro-slots" for tiny ephemeral sessions (bill per 10s) for serverless-like UX.
- Could offer reserved slot pools (monthly commit) at steep discount targeted to enterprise Dedicated customers.
- Consider credit-decay for unused credits (force usage or refunds) — dangerous, probably avoid.

Bottom line (initial gut):
- Slotized credits can expose capacity economics to customers and buy predictability for both sides, but defaults and autosuspend policies are critical to avoid sticker shock.
- Start small: hybrid approach where standard PAYG customers see only per-token billing; enable slotized plans for customers who opt-in or cross a concurrency threshold.

End of playbook sketch.

-- Asha

Notes: this doc intentionally uses several round numbers; do not baseline pricing decisions on these values without real profiling and infra cost breakdown.
